question: Which of the given sectors is largely driven by considerations of social welfare?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Public sector consists of enterprises owned and controlled by the government (central, state, or local), and its primary objective is social welfare and service to society rather than profit maximisation. (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र — समाज कल्याण)

 

• Public sector undertakings (PSUs) are typically set up to provide essential goods and services (railways, electricity, banking, healthcare, etc.) at affordable prices, to generate employment, and to promote balanced regional development.

 

• Since the state is accountable to the public, public sector enterprises prioritise the larger public interest over private profit, which distinguishes them from private enterprises.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of public sector undertakings in India include ONGC, SAIL, BHEL, Indian Railways and LIC.

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into Schedule A (exclusively public sector), Schedule B (mixed) and Schedule C (private sector), giving the public sector a dominant role in the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Foreign (Option 1): This is not a distinct ownership sector like public/private/co-operative; it refers to foreign-owned investment or enterprises operating in the domestic economy.

 

• Co-operative (Option 2): Co-operative sector enterprises are owned and run by their members for mutual benefit (e.g., Amul), not primarily for broad social welfare of the general public.

 

• Private (Option 4): The private sector is owned by individuals or private entities and is primarily driven by the motive of profit maximisation.

question: The Hindu college was established in 1791 at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banaras.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hindu College, Banaras, was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident at Banaras, with the aim of promoting the study of Hindu law, philosophy and Sanskrit literature. (हिन्दू कॉलेज, बनारस — जोनाथन डंकन)

 

• It later merged and evolved into the Government Sanskrit College, Banaras, and is considered one of the earliest institutions of higher learning established in India under colonial patronage.

 

• This college should not be confused with the more famous Hindu College, Calcutta, founded much later, in 1817.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindu College, Calcutta (1817) was founded by David Hare, Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Sir Edward Hyde East, and later became Presidency College.

 

• Banaras (Varanasi) was also later home to the Benaras Hindu University (BHU), founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta (Option 1): The Hindu College here was established in 1817, not 1791.

 

• Dacca (Option 2): Dacca (Dhaka) College was established in 1841, unrelated to this 1791 institution.

 

• Surat (Option 3): Surat has no historical Hindu College established in 1791.

question: In which of the following languages did Jyotiba Phule write ‘Gulamgiri’ in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marathi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jyotiba (Jyotirao) Phule wrote 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery) in 1873 in the Marathi language. (गुलामगिरी — ज्योतिबा फुले, मराठी भाषा)

 

• The book was dedicated to the good people of the United States for their efforts to abolish Black slavery, and it drew a parallel between the plight of the Shudras and Ati-Shudras under Brahmanical dominance and that of Black slaves in America.

 

• In the same year, 1873, Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers) to fight caste discrimination and promote social equality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jyotiba Phule is also known for his work in women's education, having started one of the first schools for girls in India in 1848 in Pune along with his wife Savitribai Phule.

 

• Other notable works by Phule include 'Sarvajanik Satyadharma' and 'Shetkarayacha Asud' (Cultivator's Whipcord).

 

NOTE

 

• English (Option 1): Gulamgiri was written directly in Marathi, not English, though it has since been translated into English.

 

• Hindi (Option 3): Phule's major works were composed in Marathi, his native language, not Hindi.

 

• Gujarati (Option 4): Gulamgiri was not written in Gujarati.

question: Which of the following are Rabi crops only?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barley and gram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–December) and harvested in spring (April–June); barley and gram (chana) are both classic Rabi crops grown in this season. (रबी फसलें — जौ और चना)

 

• Other major Rabi crops include wheat, mustard, peas and linseed, which require cool weather for germination and vegetative growth and warm weather for the ripening of grain.

 

• Rabi cultivation depends on winter rainfall (from western temperate cyclones) and irrigation, and is concentrated in states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharif crops (e.g., rice, maize, cotton, jowar, bajra) are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October.

 

• Zaid crops are short-duration summer crops grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, such as watermelon, cucumber and muskmelon.

 

NOTE

 

• Maize and peas (Option 1): Maize is primarily a Kharif crop; only peas among the two is Rabi, so this pair is not "Rabi only".

 

• Paddy and cotton (Option 3): Both paddy (rice) and cotton are Kharif crops, not Rabi.

 

• Wheat and jowar (Option 4): Wheat is Rabi, but jowar (sorghum) is predominantly a Kharif crop, so this pair is not "Rabi only".

question: Identify an example of organisms that are free-swimming and bottom-dwelling forms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zooplankton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Zooplankton are minute, largely free-floating/weakly free-swimming animal forms found in aquatic ecosystems, and many groups also occupy bottom-dwelling (benthic) habitats at various life stages, making them the example fitting both descriptions. (जूप्लैंकटन — मुक्त तैरने वाले व तलवासी जीव)

 

• Zooplankton include organisms such as protozoans, small crustaceans (like copepods and cladocerans), and the larval stages of many aquatic animals; they form a crucial link in the aquatic food chain, feeding on phytoplankton and in turn being eaten by fish.

 

• Ecologically, aquatic organisms are broadly classified into plankton (floating), nekton (strong swimmers), neuston (surface dwellers) and benthos (bottom dwellers); zooplankton overlap with both free-swimming and bottom-associated categories in many classification schemes used in school-level biology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phytoplankton are the plant-like, photosynthetic (autotrophic) organisms of the plankton community, forming the base of the aquatic food chain.

 

• Benthos is the specific ecological term for organisms that live on or in the bottom sediments of a water body, such as clams, snails and some worms.

 

NOTE

 

• Phytoplankton (Option 1): These are autotrophic, plant-like organisms; they are not classified as bottom-dwelling animal forms.

 

• Fungi (Option 3): Fungi are decomposers, not classified under free-swimming or bottom-dwelling aquatic animal groups in this context.

 

• Jellyfishes (Option 4): Jellyfish are classified as nekton/plankton (drifters) in open water; they are not typically described as bottom-dwelling forms.

question: Which of the following cities hosted the 2019 Military World Games organised by the International Military Sports Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wuhan, China.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 7th Military World Games (2019), organised by the International Military Sports Council (CISM), were held in Wuhan, China, from 18 to 27 October 2019. (सैन्य विश्व खेल 2019 — वुहान, चीन)

 

• Over 9,000 athletes from more than 100 countries participated, making it the largest edition of the Games at the time, held across newly built and upgraded sports venues in Wuhan.

 

• The Military World Games, sometimes called the "Mini Olympics for the Military", are held every four years for active-duty and reserve military personnel of CISM member nations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CISM (Conseil International du Sport Militaire) was founded in 1948 and is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium.

 

• The first Military World Games were held in 1995 in Rome, Italy; the 2023 edition was hosted by India in various cities.

 

NOTE

 

• Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Option 1): Rio hosted the 2011 Military World Games, not the 2019 edition.

 

• Bogota, Colombia (Option 2): Bogota was not a host city for the Military World Games.

 

• Mungyeong, South Korea (Option 4): Mungyeong hosted the 2015 Military World Games, not 2019.

question: Abdul Karim Khan was the exponent of which school of Hindustani Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Abdul Karim Khan (1872–1937) was the founder-exponent of the Kirana Gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music. (किराना घराना — अब्दुल करीम खान)

 

• The Kirana Gharana is named after the town of Kairana in Uttar Pradesh, from where Abdul Karim Khan's ancestors hailed, and it is known for its emphasis on sur (pitch) purity, slow tempo and meend (glide).

 

• He also founded the Arya Sangeet Vidyalaya in Pune in 1913 to teach Hindustani music, and later settled in Miraj, Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous exponents of the Kirana Gharana who followed Abdul Karim Khan include Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal and Hirabai Barodekar.

 

• Other major Hindustani vocal gharanas include the Gwalior Gharana (considered the oldest), the Agra Gharana, and the Patiala Gharana.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaipur Gharana (Option 1): Associated with Alladiya Khan, known for the Jaipur-Atrauli style of khayal singing.

 

• Gwalior Gharana (Option 2): Considered the oldest khayal gharana, associated with figures like Nathan Peer Baksh.

 

• Delhi Gharana (Option 3): Associated with musicians descended from the Mughal court tradition, distinct from the Kirana school founded by Abdul Karim Khan.

question: Who has taken oath as Bihar Chief Minister for 8th time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitish Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitish Kumar took oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the 8th time on 10 August 2022, after breaking his alliance with the BJP and forming a new government with the RJD, Congress and Left parties (the "Mahagathbandhan"). (नीतीश कुमार — बिहार के मुख्यमंत्री, 8वीं बार शपथ)

 

• With this, Nitish Kumar became the first person to take oath as Bihar Chief Minister eight separate times, spanning tenures since 2000.

 

• Tejashwi Yadav was sworn in as his Deputy Chief Minister in this same government (August 2022).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nitish Kumar first became Bihar CM briefly in 2000, and has led the state government multiple times since 2005 under various party alliances (JD(U), NDA, and Mahagathbandhan).

 

• Bihar's Governor at the time of the August 2022 oath ceremony was Phagu Chauhan.

 

NOTE

 

• Tejaswi Prasad Yadav (Option 1): He became Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar in August 2022, not the Chief Minister.

 

• Pramod Sawant (Option 2): He is the Chief Minister of Goa, not Bihar.

 

• Anugrah Narayan (Option 3): Anugrah Narayan Sinha was Bihar's first Deputy Chief Minister (post-independence era), not a Chief Minister who took oath 8 times.

question:
Which of the following statements about cell cycle is FALSE?

1. Preparation of mitosis takes place in G2 phase.

2. In M phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.

3. In S phase, replication of DNA takes place.

4. In G1 phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.
option_1: Preparation of mitosis takes place in G2 phase.
option_2: In M phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.
option_3: In S phase, replication of DNA takes place.
option_4: In G1 phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is In M phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell cycle consists of Interphase (G1, S, G2 phases) followed by the M (Mitotic) phase; the statement about M phase is false because physical growth and organelle duplication occur during G1 phase, not M phase. (कोशिका चक्र — G1, S, G2, M प्रावस्था)

 

• G1 phase (Gap 1): The cell grows in size, synthesises proteins and RNA, and duplicates its organelles — preparing for DNA synthesis.

 

• S phase (Synthesis): The cell's DNA is replicated, doubling the genetic material.

 

• G2 phase (Gap 2): The cell continues to grow and synthesises proteins needed for mitosis, effectively preparing the cell for mitosis (M phase).

 

• M phase (Mitosis): This is the actual division phase, where the duplicated chromosomes are segregated into two daughter nuclei followed by cytokinesis — it is a division phase, not a growth phase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The interphase (G1 + S + G2) constitutes about 90-95% of the total cell cycle duration, while the M phase is comparatively very short.

 

• Cells that do not divide further (e.g., neurons) exit the cycle into a resting stage called G0 phase.

 

NOTE

 

• Preparation of mitosis takes place in G2 phase (Option 1): This statement is correct, as G2 is the phase where the cell prepares directly for mitosis.

 

• In S phase, replication of DNA takes place (Option 3): This statement is correct — DNA replication is the defining event of the S phase.

 

• In G1 phase, the cell grows physically larger and copies organelles (Option 4): This statement is correct — this growth and organelle duplication is characteristic of G1, which is wrongly attributed to M phase in the false Option 2.

question: Shyamji Krishna Varma established India House at _________ in 1905.
solution_text:
The correct answer is London.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma established India House in London (Highgate) in 1905 as a hostel for Indian students and a hub for revolutionary and nationalist activities against British rule. (इंडिया हाउस — श्यामजी कृष्ण वर्मा, लंदन)

 

• In the same year, he founded The Indian Sociologist, a monthly journal, and also established the Indian Home Rule Society.

 

• India House became a centre for prominent revolutionaries such as V.D. Savarkar, Madan Lal Dhingra and Madame Bhikaji Cama, who were inspired by Shyamji Krishna Varma's nationalist ideas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma also instituted scholarships to encourage Indian students to travel to England for higher studies and revolutionary training.

 

• Madan Lal Dhingra, associated with India House, assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909.

 

NOTE

 

• New York (Option 1): India House did not exist in New York; it was a London-based institution.

 

• Bombay (Option 2): India House was established abroad in London, not in Bombay.

 

• Paris (Option 3): Madame Bhikaji Cama was active from Paris, but India House itself was established in London, not Paris.

question: ‘Indira Gandhi Shehri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana 2022’ has been implemented by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Indira Gandhi Shehri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana (IGSRGY) 2022' was launched by the Government of Rajasthan (Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot) to provide guaranteed urban employment, on the lines of MGNREGA for rural areas. (इंदिरा गांधी शहरी रोजगार गारंटी योजना — राजस्थान)

 

• The scheme guarantees 100 days of employment per year to urban households, and was later expanded (Chief Minister raised working days to 125) to widen its coverage.

 

• This scheme was announced as part of the Rajasthan State Budget 2022-23 and made Rajasthan one of the first states to guarantee employment specifically in urban areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan's urban employment scheme is modelled on the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, which guarantees rural employment nationally.

 

• Rajasthan has also implemented other welfare schemes such as the Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana and Mukhyamantri Nishulk Dava Yojana.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 2): This scheme was not implemented in Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Maharashtra did not launch this particular urban employment guarantee scheme.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): This scheme was not implemented by the Uttar Pradesh government.

question: Choose the correct pair from the following options.
option_1: Third Five-year Plan – Rapid industrialisation and basic industries
option_2: Fourth Five-year Plan - Family planning programme
option_4: Second Five-year Plan – Focus on agriculture
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fourth Five-year Plan - Family planning programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) was based on the objectives of "Growth with Stability" and "progressive achievement of self-reliance", and gave special thrust to the family planning programme to control population growth. (चतुर्थ पंचवर्षीय योजना — परिवार नियोजन कार्यक्रम)

 

• This plan was formulated under the guidance of the D.R. Gadgil model, and was implemented during a period marked by the Indo-Pak war of 1971 and the influx of refugees from Bangladesh, which strained resources.

 

• Family planning received major emphasis for the first time as a national priority in this plan period, given rising concerns over population growth undermining development gains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan is also associated with the nationalisation of 14 major banks (1969) and the Green Revolution's expansion.

 

• Five-Year Plans in India were formulated by the Planning Commission, which was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Third Five-year Plan – Rapid industrialisation and basic industries (Option 1): This description (rapid industrialisation, basic and heavy industries) actually characterises the Second Five-Year Plan, based on the Mahalanobis model.

 

• First Five-year Plan – Mahalanobis model (Option 3): The Mahalanobis model was adopted in the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), not the First.

 

• Second Five-year Plan – Focus on agriculture (Option 4): Focus on agriculture characterised the First Five-Year Plan (1951-56), based on the Harrod-Domar model, not the Second.

question: Fundamental Duties were added in the Constitution of India under the leadership of which Prime Minister of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution as Article 51A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, during the government of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 42वां संविधान संशोधन, इंदिरा गांधी)

 

• This amendment was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, which was set up to suggest amendments to the Constitution, including duties for citizens.

 

• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added (later an 11th was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, regarding education for children aged 6-14 years).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties in India are inspired by similar provisions in the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

 

• The 42nd Amendment (1976) is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it introduced, including changes to the Preamble (adding 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity').

 

NOTE

 

• Narsimha Rao (Option 1): P.V. Narasimha Rao's tenure (1991-96) is known for economic liberalisation, not the addition of Fundamental Duties.

 

• Charan Singh (Option 2): Charan Singh was Prime Minister briefly in 1979-80, not associated with the 42nd Amendment.

 

• Lal Bahadur Shastri (Option 4): Shastri was Prime Minister from 1964-66, well before the 42nd Amendment of 1976.

question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the month of August–September?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Onam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated in the Malayalam month of Chingam, which corresponds to August–September in the Gregorian calendar. (ओणम — केरल, अगस्त-सितंबर)

 

• The festival commemorates the mythical homecoming of the demon-king Mahabali, and is celebrated with Pookalam (floral rangoli), Vallam Kali (snake boat races), Onasadya (grand feast) and the Pulikali (tiger dance).

 

• It is a ten-day festival, with the tenth day, Thiru Onam, being the most significant day of celebration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Onam is celebrated by Malayalis across the world, irrespective of religion, and is considered the state festival of Kerala.

 

• Other notable harvest festivals of India include Pongal (Tamil Nadu, January), Baisakhi (Punjab, April) and Bihu (Assam, April).

 

NOTE

 

• Makar Sankranti (Option 1): This festival is celebrated in January, marking the sun's transition into Capricorn.

 

• Kite Festival (Option 2): Celebrated in January, coinciding with Makar Sankranti/Uttarayan, notably in Gujarat.

 

• Bikaner Festival (Option 3): The Bikaner Camel Festival/Bikaner Festival is celebrated in January, not August-September.

question: ‘Mission Kushal Karmi’ was launched to upgrade the skills of construction workers. This programme was launched by the government of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Mission Kushal Karmi' was launched by the Government of Delhi (Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal) to upgrade the skills of construction workers through short-term training programmes. (मिशन कुशल कर्मी — दिल्ली सरकार)

 

• The programme was launched under the aegis of the Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University (DSEU), aiming to train lakhs of construction workers registered with the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

 

• The initiative aimed to formalise and certify the skills of informal construction sector workers, improving their employability and wages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• DSEU (Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University) was established by the Delhi government in 2020 to provide skill-based higher education.

 

• The Delhi government has also run other welfare schemes for construction workers, including financial assistance and pension schemes under the Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) Welfare Board.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Mission Kushal Karmi was not launched by the Gujarat government.

 

• Haryana (Option 2): This scheme was not launched by the Haryana government.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): This scheme was not launched by the Punjab government.

question: first edition of the Youth Olympic Games was held at _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singapore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games was held in Singapore from 14 to 26 August 2010. (प्रथम युवा ओलंपिक खेल — सिंगापुर, 2010)

 

• The Youth Olympic Games (YOG) is an international multi-sport event for athletes aged between 14 and 18 years, organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), held every four years, alternating between Summer and Winter editions.

 

• The concept of the Youth Olympic Games was proposed by IOC President Jacques Rogge and approved by the IOC in 2007.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Winter Youth Olympic Games were held in Innsbruck, Austria, in 2012.

 

• The second Summer Youth Olympic Games were held in Nanjing, China, in 2014, and the third edition was held in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 2018.

 

NOTE

 

• Lausanne (Option 1): Lausanne, Switzerland, hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games in 2020, not the first edition.

 

• Nanjing (Option 3): Nanjing hosted the second edition (2014) of the Summer Youth Olympic Games, not the first.

 

• Innsbruck (Option 4): Innsbruck hosted the first Winter Youth Olympic Games (2012), not the very first (Summer) edition.

question: Thorny bushes are found in ______ region.
solution_text:
The correct answer is dry desert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thorny bushes and scrubs are characteristic vegetation of dry desert regions, where plants adapt to scarce water availability through features like reduced leaves (thorns), deep roots and thick, fleshy, water-storing stems. (कंटीली झाड़ियाँ — शुष्क मरुस्थलीय क्षेत्र)

 

• Desert vegetation such as cacti, babool (acacia) and kikar develop long roots to draw moisture from deep underground, and their leaves are reduced to thorns to minimise water loss through transpiration.

 

• This vegetation type is found in India's Thar Desert (Rajasthan) and other arid tracts of Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana receiving less than 70 cm of annual rainfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tropical evergreen forests are found in regions of very high rainfall (over 200 cm), with dense, tall trees.

 

• Mediterranean vegetation consists of evergreen shrubs and short trees adapted to hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters, found in coastal areas like California and the Mediterranean basin.

 

NOTE

 

• Mediterranean (Option 1): This region features low, evergreen shrubs suited to hot, dry summers, not thorny desert bushes.

 

• Polar (Option 2): Polar regions have very limited vegetation, mainly mosses, lichens and small shrubs (tundra vegetation), not thorny bushes.

 

• High rainfall (Option 4): High rainfall regions support dense evergreen forests, the opposite vegetation type from sparse, thorny desert scrub.

question: Which of the following folk dance forms does NOT belong to the state of Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bidesiya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bidesiya is a folk theatre/dance-drama form of Bihar (associated with the Bhojpuri-speaking region), not a folk dance of Gujarat, making it the odd one out. (बिदेसिया — बिहार की लोकनाट्य शैली)

 

• It was created by the folk poet-playwright Bhikhari Thakur and typically portrays themes of migration, separation of husbands who go abroad ('bidesh') for work, and the resulting hardships faced by their wives.

 

• In contrast, Garba, Dandiya Raas and Vinchhudo are all traditional folk dances of Gujarat, commonly performed during Navratri and other festive occasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Garba is performed in a circular pattern around a lamp or image of the Goddess (Shakti), often accompanied by clapping.

 

• Dandiya Raas is performed using decorated sticks (dandiyas) that dancers strike together rhythmically, also associated with Krishna's Raas Leela.

 

NOTE

 

• Garba (Option 1): This is a well-known traditional folk dance of Gujarat performed during Navratri.

 

• Dandiya Raas (Option 2): This is a stick dance form traditionally performed in Gujarat during Navratri festivities.

 

• Vinchhudo (Option 4): This is a traditional folk dance of Gujarat depicting a scorpion sting, performed with dramatic expressions.

question: Who among the following classical dancers was rewarded with the Padma Vibhushan Award in 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonal Mansingh, an eminent exponent of Odissi and Bharatanatyam, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2003, India's second-highest civilian award. (सोनल मानसिंह — पद्म विभूषण 2003)

 

• She had earlier received the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and is also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award; she later served as a nominated Member of the Rajya Sabha (2018-2024).

 

• Sonal Mansingh is the founder of the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi, and has been a strong advocate for the revival and promotion of India's classical dance traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna, awarded for exceptional and distinguished service.

 

• Other renowned Odissi dancers include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Madhavi Mudgal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kumudini Lakhia (Option 2): A renowned Kathak dancer, she was awarded the Padma Bhushan (2010) and Padma Shri (1987), not the Padma Vibhushan in 2003.

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 3): A noted Kathak dancer, she received the Padma Shri in 1992, not the Padma Vibhushan.

 

• Sunayana Hazarilal (Option 4): A Kathak dancer, she is not the recipient of the 2003 Padma Vibhushan Award.

question: The SI unit of acceleration is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is m/s².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time; since velocity is measured in m/s and time in s, the SI unit of acceleration is m/s² (metre per second squared). (त्वरण का SI मात्रक — मीटर/सेकंड²)

 

• Mathematically, acceleration (a) = Δv / Δt, so its unit is derived as (m/s) / s = m/s².

 

• Acceleration is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, and can be positive (speeding up) or negative/retardation (slowing down).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of velocity is m/s, and the SI unit of force (mass × acceleration) is the Newton (N) = kg·m/s².

 

• The acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².

 

NOTE

 

• m2/s (Option 1): This is not a standard unit for any common kinematic quantity such as acceleration.

 

• m2/s2 (Option 2): This unit corresponds to quantities like specific energy (energy per unit mass), not acceleration.

 

• m/s (Option 3): This is the SI unit of velocity/speed, not acceleration.

question: The Tamil word ‘muvendar’ mentioned in the Sangam poems means _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three chiefs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tamil term 'muvendar', found in Sangam literature, literally means "three chiefs" or "three crowned kings", referring collectively to the rulers of the Chera, Chola and Pandya dynasties of ancient South India. (मुवेंदर — तीन प्रमुख/तीन मुकुटधारी राजा)

 

• These three ruling lineages dominated the political landscape of the Sangam Age (roughly 300 BCE–300 CE) in present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala, and their courts were the patrons of much of the Sangam poetry that survives today.

 

• The term reflects the political structure of the age, where power was distributed among these three major chiefly/royal lineages rather than a single unified empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangam literature refers to the earliest known corpus of Tamil literature, composed over several centuries and compiled into anthologies such as the Ettuthogai and Pattupattu.

 

• Dhamma mahamatta were officials appointed by Emperor Ashoka to oversee the propagation of Dhamma — an unrelated administrative term from the Mauryan period.

 

NOTE

 

• dhamma mahamatta (Option 1): This term refers to officers of the Mauryan king Ashoka responsible for the propagation of Dhamma, unrelated to 'muvendar'.

 

• Headmen (Option 2): This does not correctly translate the meaning of 'muvendar' as used in Sangam poems.

 

• Rich (Option 3): This is not the correct meaning of 'muvendar'.

question: The Vice President of India is elected for a period of ______ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 63 and Article 66 of the Indian Constitution, the Vice President of India is elected for a term of 5 years, and is eligible for re-election. (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति — 5 वर्ष का कार्यकाल)

 

• The Vice President is elected by members of an Electoral College consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, with voting by secret ballot.

 

• The Vice President can continue to hold office even after the expiry of the 5-year term until a successor assumes charge, and can resign by tendering a resignation letter to the President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vice President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Unlike the President's election, state legislative assembly members do NOT participate in the Vice-Presidential election.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1): This is not the term of the Vice President; it does not match the constitutionally prescribed 5-year term.

 

• 2 (Option 3): This is far shorter than the actual 5-year term prescribed under the Constitution.

 

• 3 (Option 4): This is also incorrect; the Vice President's term is 5 years, not 3.

question: Which of the following is highest quality coal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anthracite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anthracite is the highest quality (highest grade) of coal, containing the highest carbon content (86-98%) and the highest calorific value, along with very low moisture and volatile matter content. (एंथ्रासाइट — सर्वोच्च गुणवत्ता वाला कोयला)

 

• Coal formation follows a sequence based on increasing carbon content and metamorphism: Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite, representing progressively higher quality and age.

 

• Anthracite burns with very little smoke and is the cleanest-burning type of coal, but it is relatively rare and found in limited quantities in India (e.g., in Jammu & Kashmir).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Peat is the first and lowest-grade stage of coal formation, with a high moisture content and low carbon content.

 

• Bituminous coal, the most commonly used type industrially and for power generation in India, has a carbon content of around 60-80%.

 

NOTE

 

• Lignite (Option 1): Also called "brown coal", it is a low-grade coal with a carbon content of about 60-70%, higher quality than peat but lower than bituminous or anthracite.

 

• Bituminous (Option 2): This is a medium-to-high grade coal, widely used for power generation and metallurgical purposes, but it ranks below anthracite in quality.

 

• Peat (Option 3): This is the lowest-grade, initial stage of coal formation with high moisture and low carbon content.

question: What are the three parts of bacterial flagellum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Filament, hook and basal body.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The bacterial flagellum is composed of three main structural parts: the filament (the long helical whip-like structure extending outside the cell), the hook (a curved connector), and the basal body (the motor structure embedded in the cell envelope). (जीवाणु कशाभिका — तंतु, हुक और आधार काय)

 

• The basal body acts as a rotary motor, anchored in the plasma membrane (and cell wall in some bacteria), and drives the rotation of the flagellum, which propels the bacterium through movement.

 

• The hook connects the filament to the basal body and helps transmit the torque generated by the motor to the filament, enabling flagellar rotation and bacterial motility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The flagellum is primarily made up of a protein called flagellin, arranged in a helical structure to form the filament.

 

• Bacterial flagella arrangement can vary — monotrichous (single flagellum), lophotrichous (tuft at one end), amphitrichous (one at each end), and peritrichous (all around the cell).

 

NOTE

 

• Head, tail and lower body (Option 1): This is not the correct terminology for the parts of a bacterial flagellum.

 

• Filament, tail and hook (Option 2): This combination incorrectly includes 'tail' instead of the actual structural component 'basal body'.

 

• Basal body, tail and filament (Option 3): This combination incorrectly includes 'tail' in place of the correct term 'hook'.

question: Common name of the compound CaOCl2 is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bleaching powder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• CaOCl₂ (Calcium oxychloride), chemically known as calcium hypochlorite, is commonly called bleaching powder. (ब्लीचिंग पाउडर — CaOCl₂, कैल्शियम ऑक्सीक्लोराइड)

 

• It is manufactured by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂) in the Backmann's process, and is widely used for bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry, and for bleaching wood pulp in paper factories.

 

• Bleaching powder is also used as a disinfectant and for water purification because of the chlorine it releases, and as an oxidising agent in various chemical industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Washing soda is chemically sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O), used in glass, soap and paper industries.

 

• Baking soda is chemically sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), commonly used in cooking and as an antacid.

 

NOTE

 

• washing soda (Option 2): Its chemical formula is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, not CaOCl₂.

 

• baking soda (Option 3): Its chemical formula is NaHCO₃, not CaOCl₂.

 

• gypsum (Option 4): Its chemical formula is CaSO₄·2H₂O (calcium sulphate dihydrate), not CaOCl₂.
